title: Rollouts: policy-first UX playbook and wireframe notes (canary, A/B, fallback)
content:
Overview:
This is a working playbook for the Rollouts console UX that centers on a policy-first mental model. Focus areas: canary deploys, multi-variant A/B tests, and automatic fallback policies when capacity/latency/quality thresholds are hit.

Why policy-first?
- Users (platform engineers, product teams) want predictable, automatable behavior rather than manual toggles.
- Policies let us express routing rules, fallback priorities, and SLO constraints in one place, then compose them into rollout strategies.
- UX should make policy implications visible (cost/latency/quality impact) at every step.

Audience / personas (short):
- Platform engineer: creates organization-wide policies, pins model versions, cares about observability and rollback speed.
- ML/product owner: running experiments (A/B), wants clear split controls and metrics tied to prompts/prompt-sets.
- App engineer: needs safe defaults, quick canary steps, and automatic fallback when capacity is constrained.

High-level goals for the console flow:
1) Make rollout creation concise: choose targets, attach policy, set metrics and guardrails, launch.
2) Visualize expected behavior (routing diagram + sample decision tree) before launch.
3) Provide realtime and historical telemetry per cohort/variant: latency, error rate, cost-per-token, quality regression (evals).
4) Support automatic remediation: auto-fallback, auto-scale hints, or pause and notify.
5) Make rollbacks trivial and auditable.

Wireframe writeups (text sketches):
--- Create Rollout (wizard) ---
Step 1: Basics panel (left) + preview panel (right)
- Name: [text]  (required)
- Description: [textarea] (optional)
- Type: radio -> {Canary, A/B test, Blue/Green (deprecated), Progressive rollout}
- Target model(s): searchable dropdown (can pick model variant tags, e.g., raven-1.3-quant, gptx-small-8bit)
- Traffic target: slider or % input (for canary: 0.5%-20%)
- Policy: attach dropdown -> {Latency SLO policy, Cost cap, Quality holdback, Custom policy} + quick badges showing matched rules
- Preview (right): diagram of routing (user -> policy -> model variant). Small sample request trace showing decision path and tokens charged.

Step 2: Guards & Metrics
- Guard rails: checkboxes and thresholds: latency p95 (ms), error rate %, cost per 1k tokens, eval metric delta.
- Auto-actions (radio group): {Pause + Notify, Auto-fallback to variant X, Scale up dedicated pool, Rollback}
- Notification targets: Slack channel / PagerDuty / Email (searchable list)
- Metrics to show in console: toggles to enable (response latency histogram, token cost histogram, model output quality sample set).

Step 3: Audience & Scheduling
- Audience: all traffic / subset by route / header / cookie / user id hashing (hash wheel preview)
- Schedule: immediate / start time / staged rollout (schedule timeline where you can add cohorts e.g., 1% -> 5% -> 25% )

Step 4: Review & Launch
- Launch preview: show expected cost delta (estimate), performance delta, and risk level (low/medium/high) with reasons (e.g., new model is quantized -> lower cost but potential quality delta).
- Confirm buttons: Launch (and open live monitoring), Save draft, Cancel

Inline helpers and tooltips:
- Small ? icons next to policy names that open the policy summary and sample JSON.
- Example prompts button: run 3 example prompts against each variant and show side-by-side outputs (quick quality check).
- "What happens if X": simulation mode to see routing for sample traces (useful for infra/ops folks).

Policy & fallback UX specifics:
- Policy builder modal: selectable blocks (SLO threshold, capacity check, region preference, priority). Composeable with AND/OR.
- Each policy block maps to an action: allow (route), block, fallback to model Y, route to backlog queue, or scale.
- Policy precedence UI: list with drag handles to reorder. Top-most rule wins. Inline evaluation examples shown below rules.

Automatic fallback flow (wireframe notes):
- When policy condition is met (e.g., p95 > 800ms or queued requests > 10k):
  1) Console displays a prominent banner on the rollout detail page: "Fallback triggered: routed X% traffic to fallback model 'raven-1.2'."
  2) Banner shows quick actions: Revert rollout | View traces | Acknowledge + silence alerts | Edit policy
  3) Audit entry created (who, when, condition matched, action taken, pre/post traffic split).
  4) If auto-scaling is configured, show pending scaling actions with ETA and a cancel button.

A/B test UX specifics:
- Variant table: name, model tag, traffic %, sample output link, key metric columns (latency p50/p95, error rate, cost/1k tokens, eval score).
- Comparison chart: side-by-side metric sparklines with statistical significance indicator (basic) and link to deeper stats page (for product analytics team).
- Quick promote button to convert winning variant into primary model (with confirm modal and preview of rollout that will happen).

Observability / monitoring placement:
- Live Rollout detail: top: Summary + traffic split badges. Middle: timeline with recent events (fallbacks, policy triggers, rollouts stages). Bottom: metric panels with per-variant breakdown and sample logs/traces.
- Links to console traces should auto-fill the rollout id and variant id.

Telemetry and events to capture (core list for SRE/product):
- rollout.create, rollout.update, rollout.launch, rollout.stage-change, rollout.fallback-triggered, rollout.rollback, rollout.promote-variant
- policy.evaluation (include matched condition id), policy.action (fallback/allow/scale), routing.decision (variant_id, reason)
- For each, capture: actor, timestamp, rollout_id, variant_ids, metric values that triggered decision

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Users can create canary rollouts with: % traffic target, attached policy, and one auto-action.
- Console displays live traffic split and recent policy triggers for each rollout.
- Auto-fallback executes and creates an auditable event with quick rollback path.
- Basic A/B flows: create 2+ variants, show per-variant metrics, and allow promoting winner.
- Unit/integration tests exist for policy evaluation UI and simulation mode.

Backlog/grooming notes (ordered):
- [P0] Policy composer UI skeleton + backend contract (PRO-2847)
- [P0] Rollout creation wizard (wizard steps 1-4 above) (PRO-2899)
- [P1] Auto-fallback banner + audit entries (PRO-2910)
- [P1] Quick example-runner: run 3 prompts across variants (frontend + ephemeral routing infra) (PRO-2932)
- [P2] Statistical significance indicator for A/B tests (integration with analytics) (PRO-2955)
- [P2] Simulation mode for routing decisions (sample traces) (PRO-2971)
- [P3] Complex audience targeting (header/cookie rules) + hash preview
- [Tech debt] Wire up rollout telemetry to BigQuery for long-term analysis

Open questions (to resolve during grooming):
- What are the exact guard metric names and units we show in the UI? (SRE: should we expose both p95 and p99?)
- How to present cost estimates reliably across models with different tokenization? (Finance involvement needed)
- Should the policy composer allow nested groups (AND of ORs) in MVP? complexity vs usefulness.
- For A/B significance, what threshold do we show by default? (Product analytics opinion needed)
- Where do we store per-rollout synthetic prompt sets (for quick-run)? per-project or global?

Copy snippets (for designers/devs):
- Launch confirmation headline: "Launch rollout: <name>"
- Risk badge: "Estimated impact: Low / Medium / High" with tooltip "Impact combines latency, cost, and eval delta"
- Fallback banner copy: "Automatic fallback activated — routing X% traffic to {fallback_name}. Reason: {condition} (view details)"

Notes to self / miscellaneous:
- Keep the top of the rollout detail as compact as possible; large graphs lower in the page. Ops want immediate visibility of active fallbacks and quick rollback buttons.
- Consider a small keyboard shortcut for "pause rollout" for power users.
- Need a small UX pattern for multi-tenant orgs: show which teams own which rollouts and any org-level policies that can override.
- Integration checklist: alerts (PagerDuty), cost export, policy JSON import/export, automation API endpoints.

Next steps (short):
1) Sync with SRE on metric names and policy conditions (meeting 2025-01-16).
2) Draft API schema for policy composer and circulate with infra (owner: Liam).
3) Designer to create mid-fidelity wireframes based on this doc (owner: Priya) — target 2025-01-22.
4) Groom backlog items with eng (Feb 3 grooming session) — prioritize P0s and split big items.

Editable checklist (for groom meeting):
- [ ] Confirm required policy blocks for MVP
- [ ] Finalize guard metric list (latency/error/cost/quality)
- [ ] Decide audience targeting scope for MVP
- [ ] Create API contract for quick-example-runner

Quick links (for reviewer convenience):
